clue.text: Accepting the consequences of confronting the players

definitions.meaning: an idiom for owning up and taking the punishment that follows
literally standing before the band or orchestra and its sound

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to the fallout of squaring up to a team or band.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means bravely taking punishment, and literally means standing turned towards the musicians.

clue.text: Rummages around over an extended period

definitions.meaning: searches about for food or supplies
read as two words, meaning for a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone rummages about for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching about for provisions, and, split in two, a phrase for a long while.

clue.text: Complete one's sentence and proceed no further

definitions.meaning: end a written sentence with its closing punctuation mark

explanation.surface: A prisoner finishes their term and then goes no further.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally ending with a period in punctuation, and figuratively halting altogether.

clue.text: Standard expected from small number joining the marines

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Junior recruits are expected to meet the marines' standard.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual benchmark or expected level, a synonym for the standard.

clue.text: He checks the quality of a bed-canopy

definitions.meaning: an inspector who tries things out
an old word for the canopy over a four-poster bed

explanation.surface: An inspector examines the quality of a four-poster's canopy.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector who trials things, and an archaic term for a canopy over a bed.

clue.text: Short cut found by current batch of public-school leavers?

definitions.meaning: a short hairstyle for women, popular in the 1920s
the year's harvest of pupils leaving Eton, the famous English boarding school

explanation.surface: This year's departing posh pupils have found a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known fee-paying 'public' school; 'crop' is both a haircut and a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cropped 1920s hairstyle named after Eton College, and punningly that school's yearly harvest of leavers.

clue.text: International body anticipated surprising outcome

definitions.note: used as a noun, as in 'expect the ...'

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
expected means anticipated

explanation.surface: The United Nations predicted a shock result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not foreseen is a surprising result.

clue.text: Imprisoned frequently, I take note at the critical moment

parts.note: 'in the nick' is British slang for in prison
oft is an old word for often
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A frequent jailbird jots down something just at the crucial point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the nick' is British slang for prison; 'take note' looks like writing something down.
explanation.definitionFit: Just in time, at the last possible instant before it is too late.

clue.text: Left previous editor to give it support

indicators.note: in a down clue the next piece sits beneath and holds up the one above

parts.note: ex means former or previous
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former editor quit to back the project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' works because in a down answer ED sits under IT, propping it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Went out or departed, a synonym for left as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Comments made about proficiency awards

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word meaning concerning
marks are scores awarded for skill in a test

explanation.surface: Feedback is given on how certificates of competence are handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken observations are synonyms for comments people make.

clue.text: Make excessive demands on duty and endurance

definitions.text: Make excessive demands on duty and endurance

parts.words: Make excessive demands on duty and endurance
parts.note: reads as levying too much tax, and also as straining someone's stamina too far

explanation.surface: A boss asks too much of loyalty and staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from one verb: tax as a levy (duty) and tax as a strain on stamina, each taken too far.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy too heavily, or to strain someone's strength beyond its limit.

clue.text: Daring to reveal the inner parts

definitions.meaning: courage or nerve, in an informal sense
the intestines or innards of a body or machine

explanation.surface: Showing your innards takes nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for courage, and also the plural word for intestines or inner workings.

clue.text: Discerning enough to print piece only after emendation

indicators.note: emendation is correction of a text, so these words are rewritten into new order

explanation.surface: An editor is astute enough to publish an article only once it has been corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after emendation' signals rearranging the letters of PRINT and PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Perceptive and insightful people are synonyms for discerning ones.

clue.text: Set right an inaccurate alignment

parts.note: describes correcting something that is crooked, so it lines up true

explanation.surface: A mechanic corrects a wheel that is out of true.
explanation.definitionFit: To make level or true something that is crooked or bent.

clue.text: Very little can be fitted into a filthy home

indicators.note: one word is put inside another, as a tin is fitted into a room

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a proverbially dirty dwelling
taken as written

explanation.surface: Barely anything can be squeezed into a squalid dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre or scarce, synonyms for very little.

clue.text: A divine infant, perhaps, to his baptismal sponsors

definitions.text: A divine infant, perhaps, to his baptismal sponsors

parts.words: A divine infant, perhaps, to his baptismal sponsors
parts.note: reads like the holy child, but means a baby in relation to the people who stood for it at christening

explanation.surface: A baby seems heaven-sent to those who sponsored its baptism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine infant' suggests the Christ child; the word divine here hints at the god- prefix that godparents give the child they sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Godparents sponsor a child at baptism, and that child is so called in relation to them.

clue.text: Sailor involved in racial trouble in Italy

definitions.note: a definition by location: a place found within the country

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped up inside another
trouble stirs these letters up into disorder

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman gets caught up in race-related unrest in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges RACIAL to CALRIA, and 'involved in' puts AB inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The region forming the toe of the Italian boot, located within that country.

clue.text: Father accepts our method to dispose of liquid waste

indicators.note: one word takes another inside it, as a father accepts a guest

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
taken as written
a way is a manner or method of doing something

explanation.surface: Dad takes on the family's system for getting rid of sewage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipping liquid out of a container to get rid of it, a phrasal verb.

clue.text: Bomb placed by blue-eyed boy on a public highway

parts.note: a favourite, or teacher's pet
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A favourite lad leaves an explosive on a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue-eyed boy' is British slang for someone's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A small historical explosive device for blasting open gates, as in 'hoist with his own'.

clue.text: Mug of ale containing a little potassium

indicators.note: one word holds others inside it, as a mug holds drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
K is the chemical symbol for potassium, little meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: A pint of ale has a trace of a chemical element in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking vessel, a synonym for a tall cup.

clue.text: Takes stock, with disastrous results

indicators.note: disastrous suggests things wrecked and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone reviews their inventory and the outcome is a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes stock' looks like reviewing inventory but means stealing livestock; 'disastrous' rearranges RESULTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing cattle or horses, livestock being stock.

clue.text: Annoyed when given only tea as sustenance

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
given food as sustenance means fed

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated at getting nothing but a cuppa to live on.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritated or rubbed up the wrong way, a synonym for vexed.

clue.text: A daily paper takes years to develop a communications system

parts.note: the Telegraph is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper spends years developing a way to send messages.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph is a London daily, and the setter's own paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending messages over distance by wire, a system of long-distance signalling.

clue.text: Some of the deft swimmers are salamanders

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some agile swimmers turn out to be amphibians.
explanation.definitionFit: Newts in their land stage are small salamander-like amphibians.

clue.text: Small hat refused to stay in place!

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A little cap would not stay on someone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Moved smoothly out of position, past tense of glide-like movement.

clue.text: It moves around this way and that

indicators.note: the word reads identically forwards and backwards, either way you look

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something spins about in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this way and that' tells you the answer is a palindrome, reading the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that turns or spins about an axis.

clue.text: After autumn I shall receive a complaint

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first, as the clue says

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
I'll is the contraction of I shall

explanation.surface: Someone vows to lodge a grievance once the autumn comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance, but means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness, so receiving one is becoming sick.

clue.text: Public worker sensed exceptional generosity

parts.note: open means public, not private
a hand is a manual worker

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so these letters break their usual order

explanation.surface: A civil servant detected remarkable kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: Freely giving with an unclenched palm, a synonym for liberality.
